nodes.label: Holding-period investigation
nodes.rationale: Compares seven holding deadlines with price exits retained or disabled, across three fixtures, on the same known FTFT entry. Forty-two counterfactual cells remain one underlying opportunity.

nodes.label: Retained-stop precedence over longer deadlines
nodes.rationale: The original stop requested sale at 727.588547403 seconds, before the fifteen-minute maximum. Extending the deadline to thirty minutes, sixty minutes or pre-close therefore preserves exactly the same stop execution and loss; a longer maximum does not disable earlier triggers.

nodes.label: Timer-only holding horizons
nodes.rationale: With price exits disabled, two minutes earns $35.754, fifteen minutes loses $63.726, sixty minutes loses $105.016, and close minus sixty seconds earns $642.964 nominally. The near-close outcome requires almost six hours and seven future quote-linked fills; longer holding is not consistently better.

nodes.label: Exposed pre-close analysis and incomplete adverse marks
nodes.rationale: The pre-close horizon was included after later marks were inspected, so freezing executions did not make the study independent validation. Worst pre-request marks neither model full liquidation nor measure peak-to-trough account drawdown; an approximately 300-second archived quote gap leaves unobserved losses unknown. Overnight carry was not modeled.
